findings.evidence: Proof body: `hX' : ∫ ω, fourier n (X ω) ∂P = anisotropyCoeff μ n`, `hY' : ∫ ω, fourier n (Y ω) ∂P = anisotropyCoeff μ n`, then `simp only [integral_conj, hX', hY', Complex.mul_conj']`; `IndepFun.integral_fun_comp_mul_comp` (Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Integration.lean:380) places no condition on the laws. Roadmap README.md:1099-1105 needs pair expectations for harmonic modulation plus non-flow clusters.
findings.fix: State `(hX : HasLaw X μ P) (hY : HasLaw Y ν P) : ∫ ω, fourier n (X ω) * conj (fourier n (Y ω)) ∂P = anisotropyCoeff μ n * conj (anisotropyCoeff ν n)` with the same proof minus the final `Complex.mul_conj'`; at the single use site in `integral_norm_qVector_sq` (`hjk`) close with `Complex.mul_conj'`.
findings.issue: `integral_fourier_mul_conj_fourier` requires `HasLaw X μ P` and `HasLaw Y μ P` with the same `μ`, but the proof computes `hX'` and `hY'` separately and never uses equality of laws. The general two-law form has the identical proof and is what mixed-distribution pairs (§5.3 non-flow clusters) need.

findings.evidence: Proof uses `(hφ j).integral_comp` and `integrable_fourier_comp (hφ j).aemeasurable n`; `HasLaw.integral_comp` (Mathlib/Probability/HasLaw.lean:171) has no `IsProbabilityMeasure` hypothesis, and `integrable_fourier_comp` (Mathematics/Analysis/Fourier/AddCircle.lean) requires only `[IsFiniteMeasure P]`. By contrast `integral_norm_qVector_sq` genuinely needs `P univ = 1` for the constant term.
findings.fix: Move `integral_qVector` above the `variable [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (hφ ...) (hind ...)` line, inside the `Integrable` section with `[IsFiniteMeasure P]`, taking `hφ : ∀ j, HasLaw (φ j) μ P` explicitly.
findings.issue: `integral_qVector` is declared after `variable [IsProbabilityMeasure P]` and so carries that instance, but its proof only uses integrability (`integrable_fourier_comp`, needing `IsFiniteMeasure P`) and `HasLaw.integral_comp`, which needs no measure class.

summary: The statements are mostly at the natural level (pairwise IndepFun, arbitrary measures for anisotropyCoeff, Measure.pi derived as a corollary). Two assumptions are stronger than their proofs use: the pair-expectation lemma needlessly forces equal laws, and integral_qVector inherits IsProbabilityMeasure where IsFiniteMeasure suffices.
